prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim. Injury: concussion. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1246; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim received by phone from the claimant regarding a low-speed head-on collision at a residential intersection. Claimant reports being the driver of the vehicle traveling northbound. Other vehicle was a sedan, driver reports no major damage to either vehicle. Police report requested, not yet on file. Claimant states they experienced headache and dizziness after impact and was evaluated at an urgent care facility. Claimant is not represented by an attorney at this time.

Entry 2: Recorded statement taken from claimant. Claimant describes airbag deployment and says they hit their head on the side window. Reports ongoing headache, light sensitivity, and difficulty concentrating at work. Medical provider has diagnosed a concussion and recommended rest and a follow-up in two weeks. Claimant asked how the injury portion of the claim is handled and was given the general process for bodily injury evaluation. No representation noted.

Entry 3: Obtained vehicle damage photos from the claimant's repair shop. Front bumper, hood, and radiator support show moderate deformation consistent with a low-speed impact. Estimator notes the airbags did deploy on claimant's vehicle. Other driver's insurer has been contacted to confirm liability position and coverage limits. Their adjuster indicated liability is under review pending the police report.

Entry 4: Received medical records from the urgent care visit. Diagnosis listed as mild concussion with no fracture on imaging. Restrictions include limited screen time and no driving until cleared. Claimant confirmed by phone that they have not yet retained counsel and prefers to communicate directly. Advised claimant that a rental vehicle may be available under their coverage if they require one, subject to policy terms.

Entry 5: Follow-up call with claimant. Symptoms are improving slightly but headaches persist. Claimant has a neurology appointment scheduled and will forward those records when available. Reviewed claim status with claimant, including next steps for the property damage and injury portions of the file. Diary set for review once the police report and neurology records are received. File remains open.
